correctness.rationale: For each strip, coordinate u=2^j(1-x) is uniform on [1,2); a binary first digit fixes a one- or two-step gain, with next normalized coordinate 2(u-1) mod 1. Independent digits give renewal waiting times one or two. Splitting the two half-strips yields the recurrence for every real \(s>0\) with integrable and explicitly evaluated initial conditions. The positive Perron root dominates the negative root. Strong law and inverted renewal CLT imply rate 2/3 and variance 2/27. After two steps \(x\ge1/2\); the same-y transport coupling and 1-Lipschitz distance function give exact W1. The displayed closed form is checked algebraically. A standalone Fraction script independently matches the all-strip exact integrals for four integer orders and eleven times and checks binary waiting clocks; finite tests are corroboration, not a proof of infinite claims.

value.rationale: The source gives a qualitative example of focusing under pure local isometries, an atypical situation in which contraction-based estimates are absent and a weak limit is not invariant. The theorem measures this phenomenon exactly: the moment spectrum, sharp Wasserstein rate and initial-condition Gaussian fluctuations form a unified quantitative description. It exhibits a nontrivial gap between the typical \(2^{-2/3}\) contraction factor and the average (1+sqrt(17))/8, and the precise transport identity can guide studies of concentration of discontinuous, non-invertible maps without invariant measures. The fact is intrinsic to the originating natural example, not an arbitrary finite slice or table recomputation.
